questions.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}y\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{2}y[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}y{[-\operatorname{cos}⁡x]}_{0}^{\pi /2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}y[-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{cos}⁡0]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}y\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}y\,\text{d}y & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{2}}{2}-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =2-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}[{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}{[-\frac{1}{x}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}(-\frac{1}{2}-(-1))\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1/2}\frac{1}{2\sqrt{1-{y}^{2}}}\text{d}y & =\frac{1}{2}[\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y]_{0}^{1/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(\frac{1}{2})-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{\pi }{6}-0) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{12}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant. 

Making a substitution $x+y=u,$ $\text{d}x=\text{d}u,$ we get.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x+y)^{2}}\,\text{d}x\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{(x+y)^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{y}^{1+y}\frac{1}{{u}^{2}}\,\text{d}u]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{[-\frac{1}{u}]}_{y}^{1+y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(-\frac{1}{y+1}+\frac{1}{y})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[\frac{1}{y}-\frac{1}{y+1}]\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}[\frac{1}{y}-\frac{1}{y+1}]\,\text{d}y & =[\operatorname{ln}⁡y-\operatorname{ln}⁡(y+1)]_{1}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{y}{y+1}){|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(2) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{2}{3}\cdot 2) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{4}{3})\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}[{\int }_{1/3}^{\sqrt{3}/3}\frac{3}{{y}^{2}(1+9{x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}[{\int }_{1/3}^{\sqrt{3}/3}\frac{3}{(1+(3x)^{2})}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}[\operatorname{arctan}⁡(3x)]_{1/3}^{\sqrt{3}/3}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3})-\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1))\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}(\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{\pi }{12{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1/3}^{1/4}\frac{\pi }{12{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & ={[-\frac{\pi }{12y}]}_{1/3}^{1/4} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{12\cdot \frac{1}{4}}+\frac{\pi }{12\cdot \frac{1}{3}} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{12}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}(1+{x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\frac{1}{(1+{x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}[\operatorname{arctan}⁡x]_{0}^{\sqrt{3}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡\sqrt{3}-\operatorname{arctan}⁡0)\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}(\frac{\pi }{3}-0)\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{\pi }{3{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}\frac{\pi }{3{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y & ={[-\frac{\pi }{3y}]}_{-2}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{3\cdot (-1)}-(-\frac{\pi }{3\cdot (-2)}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \frac{\pi }{4}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}[{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,[\operatorname{sin}⁡x]_{0}^{\pi /2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y(1-0)\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /4}2\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}y & =-2[\operatorname{cos}⁡y]_{0}^{\pi /4} \\  & =-2(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =-2\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}-2\cdot (-1) \\  & =2-\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}y{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 4}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}y{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{4}[{\int }_{0}^{1}y{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}[{\int }_{0}^{1}y{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{4}[{e}^{xy}]_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}({e}^{1\cdot y}-{e}^{0\cdot y})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}({e}^{y}-1)\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}({e}^{y}-1)\text{d}y & =[{e}^{y}-y]_{0}^{4} \\  & =({e}^{4}-4)-({e}^{0}-0)\text{ } \\  & ={e}^{4}-4-1 \\  & ={e}^{4}-5\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}xy\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 1}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}xy\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}xy\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}xy\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y[{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}y(\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{y}{2}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{y}{2}\,\text{d}y & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{{1}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le 2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:   

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[{e}^{x+y}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({e}^{1+y}-{e}^{0+y})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}({e}^{1+y}-{e}^{y})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(e{e}^{y}-{e}^{y})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{y}(e-1)\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{y}(e-1)\text{d}y & =(e-1)[{e}^{y}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =(e-1)({e}^{2}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =(e-1)({e}^{2}-1) \\  & ={e}^{3}-{e}^{2}-e+1\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the double integral ${∬}_{D}\frac{{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}A,$ where 
$D={(x,y)\,:\,{e}^{2}\le x\le {e}^{4},\,0\le y\le \sqrt[3]{6}}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:      

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}[{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}[{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{{y}^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}{y}^{2}[{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}{y}^{2}[\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}{y}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡{e}^{4}-\operatorname{ln}⁡{e}^{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}{y}^{2}\cdot 2\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}}2{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y & =\frac{2}{3}[{y}^{3}]_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{6}} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}((\sqrt[3]{6})^{3}-{0}^{3}) \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following equalities are true given that
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le \sqrt{2},\,-\sqrt{3}\le y\le 2}.$

- ${∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{2}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$
- ${∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$
- ${∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$
questions.worked_solution:
We notice that:  

- the limits for the variable $x$ are from $0$ to $\sqrt{2}$, and

- the limits for the variable $y$ are from $-\sqrt{3}$ to $2.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the region of integration is rectangular, we can simply swap the order of integration. This gives

$$
{∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}[{\int }_{-\sqrt{3}}^{2}\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x.
$$

So, the correct answer is "I and II only".

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant. 

Making a substitution $xy=u,$ $\text{d}y=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}u,$ we get.

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{1}x{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x[{\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{xy}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x[{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{1}{x}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{x}{e}^{u}\,\text{d}u]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{e}^{u}]_{0}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{x}-1)\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}({e}^{x}-1)\,\text{d}x & =[{e}^{x}-x]_{0}^{1} \\  & =(e-1)-(1-0) \\  & =e-2\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following equalities are true given that
$D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,\frac{1}{2}\le y\le 1}.$

- ${∬}_{D}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}A={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y$
- ${∬}_{D}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}A={\int }_{1/2}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$
- ${∬}_{D}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\text{d}A={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{1/2}^{1}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x$
questions.worked_solution:
We notice that:

- the limits for the variable $x$ are from $1$ to $2$, and

- the limits for the variable $y$ are from $\frac{1}{2}$ to $1.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{1/2}^{1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the region of integration is rectangular, we can simply swap the order of integration. This gives

$$
{∬}_{D}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}A={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{1/2}^{1}y\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x.
$$

So, the correct answer is "III only".

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:  

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}[{\int }_{1}^{2}(x+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}\,{[xy+\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}[(2x+\frac{8}{3})-(x+\frac{1}{3})]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(x+\frac{7}{3})\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(x+\frac{7}{3})\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+\frac{7x}{3}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{7}{3})-(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{7}{3}) \\  & =\frac{14}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{{e}^{-1}}^{{e}^{3}}\frac{{3}^{x}}{y}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{3}^{x}[{\int }_{{e}^{-1}}^{{e}^{3}}\frac{1}{y}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{3}^{x}[\operatorname{ln}⁡y]_{{e}^{-1}}^{{e}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{3}^{x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡{e}^{3}-\operatorname{ln}⁡{e}^{-1})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{3}^{x}(3+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4\cdot {3}^{x}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}4\cdot {3}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =4{[\frac{{3}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4(\frac{{3}^{1}-{3}^{0}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}) \\  & =\frac{8}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{4}[{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{{x}^{3}}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}{[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}]}_{0}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}(\frac{{2}^{4}}{4}-\frac{{0}^{4}}{4})\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{4}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =4{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{1}{{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.problem:
Evaluate the double integral $\displaystyle \iint \limits_{D} \dfrac y{x^2} \, \textrm d A$, where 
$D=\left\{ (x,y) \: : \:2 \leq x \leq 4,\: 0 \leq y \leq 3\right\}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:    

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{2}^{4}\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[-\frac{y}{x}]}_{2}^{4}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(-\frac{y}{4}-(-\frac{y}{2}))\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{y}{4}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{y}{4}\,\text{d}y & ={[\frac{{y}^{2}}{8}]}_{0}^{3} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{2}}{8}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{8} \\  & =\frac{9}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Which of the following equalities are true given that
$D = \big\{ (x,y) \: : \: 0 \leq x \leq 2, \: 0 \leq y \leq 1 \big\}.$

- $\displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} e^{\sqrt{xy}} \,\text{d}A  = \int_{0}^{1}  \int_{0}^{2}e^{\sqrt{xy}}\,  \text{d}y \, \text{d}x$

- $\displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} e^{\sqrt{xy}}\,\text{d}A  = \int_{0}^{2}  \int_{0}^{1} e^{\sqrt{xy}}\, \text{d}y\,  \text{d}x$

- $\displaystyle \iint\limits_{D} e^{\sqrt{xy}} \,\text{d}A = \int_{0}^{1}  \int_{0}^{2}e^{\sqrt{xy}}\,  \text{d}x \, \text{d}y$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We notice that: 

- the limits for the variable $x$ are from ${\color{blue}0}$ to ${\color{blue}2}$, and

- the limits for the variable $y$ are from ${\color{red}0}$ to ${\color{red}1}.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{e}^{\sqrt{xy}}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{0}^{2}{e}^{\sqrt{xy}}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the region of integration is rectangular, we can simply swap the order of integration. This gives

$$
\iint\limits_{D} e^{\sqrt{xy}} \,\text{d}A  
= \int_{\color{blue}0}^{\color{blue}{2}} \left[ \int_{\color{red}0}^{\color{red}1} e^{\sqrt{xy}}\,\text{d}{\color{red}y} \right] \text{d}{\color{blue}x} .
$$

So, the correct answer is "II and III only".
